response.sql:
WITH customer_orders AS (
  SELECT c.customer_id, c.gender, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count
  FROM Customers AS c
  LEFT JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  WHERE c.gender IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.gender
), customer_shares AS (
  SELECT customer_id, gender, order_count,
         1.0 * order_count / NULLIF(SUM(order_count) OVER (PARTITION BY gender), 0) AS share
  FROM customer_orders
), scored AS (
  SELECT customer_id, gender, order_count, share,
         share - AVG(share) OVER () AS gap_above_average
  FROM customer_shares
)
SELECT customer_id, gender, order_count, share, gap_above_average
FROM scored
WHERE share > (SELECT AVG(share) FROM customer_shares)
ORDER BY gap_above_average DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Customers without a recorded gender are excluded; a missing gender means NULL. Shares are each customer's orders divided by all orders for that gender, and the average is the unweighted mean share across customers with recorded gender. A gender group with no orders has an undefined share and is excluded from the above-average comparison because its shares are NULL.
